source.title: The Expressive Power of Tuning Only the Normalization Layers
source.authors: Angeliki Giannou; Shashank Rajput; Dimitris Papailiopoulos

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and experiment details.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments training only BatchNorm parameters in frozen random networks and measures loss against a target network, bearing on whether gradient-based training succeeds under the proposed conditions. It also reports constructive parameter settings, but the paper's theoretical results do not involve training.
record.gate_note: Theoretical reconstruction results are not gradient-based training results. The experiments report BatchNorm-SGD loss; cited empirical claims from Frankle et al. are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study investigates normalization parameters' expressive power and synthetic teacher reconstruction with frozen random weights. It does not compare training speed or learning-rate tolerance with versus without BatchNorm, so it does not test V6. Its constructive existence proofs and restricted-parameter SGD experiments do not test V1–V5 either.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors prove exact reconstruction through normalization parameters under sufficient overparameterization, including sparse and deeper constructions. Their synthetic experiments show advantages for constructive methods in several conditions, with width- and sparsity-dependent exceptions. They explicitly distinguish expressive capacity from gradient-based learnability and leave whether SGD can fully exploit that capacity open.
record.recipe_differences: The theoretical results construct normalization parameters to exactly realize a target network; experiments compare this with SGD training only BatchNorm parameters on synthetic teacher data. It does not use the benchmark training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with width and sparsity: SGD performs better at smaller widths in the width sweep; at 5% nonzero weights none of the methods achieves small loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Constructively chosen normalization parameters can exactly realize a smaller target ReLU network using frozen random weights, with width/depth tradeoffs and sparse-weight extensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization-layer affine parameters alone have substantial representational capacity under sufficient overparameterization; this existence result does not guarantee gradient-based learnability.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic reconstruction loss depends on parameter-setting method, width, and sparsity. Constructive methods outperform BatchNorm-only SGD in the reported dense comparison and at larger widths; SGD performs better at smaller widths and in extremely sparse settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In frozen random ReLU networks, BatchNorm-only SGD need not attain the reconstruction performance available through constructive parameter settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted for presentation at the Conference on Learning Theory (COLT) 2023.
record.problems: Synthetic teacher-network experiment rather than benchmark classification tasks; reports loss rather than training classification error or accuracy speed. Numerical results are presented in figures without exact values in the text. Only five repeats are reported, with the largest and smallest losses discarded for error bars. No explicit control condition is described.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted; four rows capture the separately reported dense and sparse experiment conditions and the width sweep.

untested.parts: Training classification error of sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels, and the stated smaller-model and regularization qualifications.
Spurious-local-minimum frequency under gradient descent as teacher/student widths grow together, and its reduction with one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain convolutional networks and prevention through identity shortcuts; the special-initialization and normalization-free qualifications.
Comparisons of activation-matched initialization schemes, signal/gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a stability threshold, transient loss growth, curvature evolution, recovery, and divergence.
Accuracy or convergence speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without BatchNorm, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V6 limits_scope verdict: the required BatchNorm-versus-no-BatchNorm speed and learning-rate comparisons are untested, not failed. Prior benchmark and optimization findings discussed in the introduction and related work are cited results, not this study's evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random labels, and does not report training classification error for benchmark classifiers.
No two-layer teacher-student ReLU local-minimum study or neuron-width comparison.
Does not compare plain and residual networks across depth for training error.
Does not compare initialization schemes for training speed or trainable depth.
Does not test learning rates relative to a stability limit or report curvature and loss dynamics under such rates.
Tests BatchNorm-only SGD on synthetic teacher-network data, but not accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance on MNIST, CIFAR-10, or ImageNet, nor Fixup.

reader_labels.condition: Synthetic teacher-network experiments with BatchNorm-only SGD and dense or sparse frozen random weights
reader_labels.reason: Training only BatchNorm parameters is compared on synthetic teacher-generated data; the text says the SGD baseline is beaten by constructive methods, and at 5% nonzero weights none achieve small loss. Rows R1–R4 report loss, not the version's benchmark accuracy-speed and learning-rate-tolerance outcomes.
